items.note: Lemon hero band with a 96px medium grotesk headline, a black CTA and five ink-outlined objects (pencil, bookmark, envelope, mug, notepad) cropped at the edges, then ink-framed white cards on paper and a black newsletter footer. It is clearly the reference's language, but the stickers are thinner, smaller line drawings than the reference's chunky extruded coins, so the hero has less of their weight and joy.

The lemon band stacks the headline, lead and black CTA with stickers shrunk and cropped at the band edges, as in the reference's mobile pricing band, and a circle vignette with an overlapping white caption pill follows. The type scale and gutters are close to the reference's phone rhythm.

The chrome inverts while the lemon band and stickers stay the same, the CTA turns pink and the current nav pill turns white, exactly as in the reference's dark capture. The cards sit black on a dark grey ground with 35% white hairlines, which reads a little flatter than the reference's all-black ground.
Same dark inversion on the phone: unchanged lemon band and stickers, a pink CTA with an ink border, and the vignette card on black with a white caption pill. Close to the reference's dark treatment.

A lemon header band carries the breadcrumb, a bold article title, meta and outline chips over a paper prose column with a ruled ink 'on this page' box, and the page ends on a pink closing band and a black footer, as the spec's band stack lays out. The weak spot is the inline figure, a generic mountain-and-sun placeholder in a periwinkle box rather than flat ink drawing.

The header band and ruled ink table-of-contents box hold up well at phone width with 48px-plus rows. The breadcrumb wraps so that the separator starts its own line, which is cruder than the reference's one-line breadcrumb.

The lemon header band and pink closing band are unchanged, and the prose, the table-of-contents box and the related cards invert to black boxes with light hairlines. It follows the reference's 'invert only the chrome' dark mode.
Lemon band over a dark ground with a black ruled table-of-contents box. It matches the light version's structure and the reference's dark behaviour; the breadcrumb wraps the same way as in light.

Same article system: a lemon title band, a prose column on paper, a ruled table-of-contents box, a white quote panel, a grey code block, related cards and a pink closing band. It is considered and on-language, but it repeats the generic mountain-and-sun placeholder figure where the reference would use a flat ink drawing.

The band, the table-of-contents box, the prose and the ruled related cards stack cleanly at a comfortable phone measure. The code block scrolls inside its frame; spacing and type stay close to the reference's mobile rhythm.
The lemon band stays as it is, the header turns black and the table-of-contents box becomes black with light rules. The hierarchy matches light mode and the reference's dark approach.
The lemon title band with outline chips is followed by a black ruled table-of-contents box on a dark ground. The inversion is faithful and the rows are comfortably tall.

A periwinkle header band holds the title, a lead and one small envelope sticker, followed by plain prose and three white author cards with periwinkle initial squares. The band's text column starts left of the body column, and the lone uncropped sticker and plain cards make it noticeably thinner and more generic than the reference's composed bands.

On the phone the periwinkle band with its envelope sticker cropped at the right edge works better, but the page below is plain prose with no further drawn structure. It is related to the reference, but quieter and more generic.
The periwinkle band and sticker are unchanged, the current pill turns white and the body inverts. It carries the same misaligned band column and sparse composition as light mode.
Periwinkle band over dark prose: a correct inversion, but the same thin, mostly typographic page as light mode, with little of the reference's poster character.

findings.summary: Article inline figures are a generic mountain-and-sun image placeholder in a band-colored box, not the system's flat ink-outlined drawing, so the one illustrative moment in a long article reads as stock wireframe art.
Hero stickers are thin, mid-size line drawings with little extrusion; the reference's objects are big chunky die-cut shapes with a thick rim that dominate the band corners.

On the about page the header band's title and lead start on a different left edge than the body column below, and its one small sticker floats uncropped, so the band feels unanchored next to the reference's aligned, composed bands.
On phones the header-band breadcrumb wraps so the separator begins its own line under the parent link.
